raw_decisions.rationale: True untrusted origin: B64Postprocessor processes the rendered HTML of untrusted Markdown; m.group('path')[1:-1] in repl_path extracts the attacker-supplied src value (quotes stripped), which flows into util.parse_url -> util.url2path -> os.path.join/normpath -> open(file_name, 'rb') at b64.py:86. The value is fully attacker-controlled string content from the Markdown document, not an internal wrapper artifact.

Host-library input boundary: the Python-Markdown core invokes B64Postprocessor.run(text) with the rendered output of untrusted Markdown source; the host call site is outside the CodeQL database, so this parameter (position 1, self slot included) is the visible entry point of the attacker-controlled text that feeds the src extraction at b64.py:73.

External semi-trusted content: tags[user_input]['zipball_url'] is read out of json.loads(requests.get(GitHub API releases).text); the basename of this URL is embedded into the downloaded-zip file path. This is not a normal untrusted input boundary (HTTPS GitHub API response, maintainer-run dev tool, user_input only selects a list index), so it is held at candidate pending human review rather than confirmed tp.

argparse CLI of a maintainer dev tool: all options (--tag, --gemoji, --twemoji, ...) are tag/version strings and booleans, not filesystem paths; the tool is operator-run and no untrusted path value is born here. Not a Pass 1 source.

The m.group('path') value is genuinely attacker-controlled (href/src attribute of untrusted rendered output), but pathconverter.py is verified pure string rewriting: no exists/open/stat or any filesystem API anywhere in the module; the rewritten value is written back into the output HTML text. No Pass 1 filesystem sink is reachable from this origin.

Same situation as the repl_relative branch: m.group('path') at repl_absolute extracts an attacker href/src value, but the module performs string rewriting only (path2url/urlunparse write-back at :107-:118) with no filesystem access; no Pass 1 sink downstream.

The host-library boundary is real (run(text) receives the untrusted rendered output at position 1, self slot included), but the whole module is verified string-only: no filesystem operation exists downstream, so this boundary cannot produce a path-traversal flow in Pass 1.

Trusted operator CLI: parse_args() of the test runner; --update/--test-target/--file are chosen by the developer running the tests. An operator is an authorized, trusted user, not an attacker boundary; no untrusted value is born here.

args.file[0] is the operator's own --file selection, canonicalized with os.path.abspath and only forwarded to test_syntax.set_target_file; this is deliberate authorized access to a test file chosen by the trusted operator, not attacker-controlled input.

download(url) receives a Markdown-controlled http(s) URL, but it is consumed by urllib.request.urlopen - a network fetch (SSRF / Pass 3 territory), not a filesystem path API. No Pass 1 traversal flow; recorded here so Pass 3 labeling can pick this boundary up.

Internal recursive entry: parse_snippets(lines) receives either the document lines from run() (the true host boundary at :352) or snippet file lines on recursion (:333-341); the parameter carries attacker text, but the origin rows at :258/:276 already model the birth of the controlled path. Kept as a low-priority source for recall of nested-include flows; primary boundary is run().

THE snippet include-path origin: m.group('snippet') returns the quoted include path straight out of the untrusted Markdown line (--8<-- inline syntax); quotes are stripped ([1:-1]) and the value flows to get_snippet_path -> os.path.join -> codecs.open. Two identical CSV rows (the two m.group('snippet') calls of the inline conditional on line 258) were deduplicated into this single entry.

Block-form include path re-extracted after suffix stripping: RE_SNIPPET_FILE removes :lines/:section suffixes and m.group(1) yields the bare attacker path from the Markdown block body; it feeds the same get_snippet_path -> join -> codecs.open flow as the inline form.

Host-library input boundary: the Python-Markdown core calls SnippetPreprocessor.run(lines) with the untrusted document source; the host invocation is outside the database, so this parameter (position 1, self slot included) is the visible entry of the attacker-controlled Markdown text whose include lines birth the paths at :258/:276.

Decode/propagation helper, not a guard: util.parse_url HTML-entity-decodes (html.unescape) and urlparse()s the attacker src value; the path component is returned and joined at b64.py:80. Required taint step (argument 0 -> parsed path component); it widens the input surface (entity-encoded traversal chars decode before the join), never restricts it.

Percent-decode step: util.url2path calls url2pathname, so %2e%2e%2f decodes into plain ../ BEFORE os.path.join at b64.py:80. Taint-preserving and traversal-enabling; explicitly NOT a sanitizer in this implementation.

os.path.normpath on the absolute branch: parse_url flags file://, c:/, // UNC and leading-/\\ forms as is_absolute, and this branch normpaths the path WITHOUT joining base_path and WITHOUT any containment check - any absolute path on the host reaches open() at :86 directly. Taint-preserving step; normpath collapses '..' lexically but enforces nothing here.

os.path.normpath over join(base_path, path): collapses '..' segments lexically but performs no base-directory containment, so sequences that normalize outside base_path still pass the exists() gate at :82 and reach open() at :86. Taint-preserving step, not a sanitizer.

os.path.join(base_path, path) composes the operator-configured base with the attacker path at argument 1: no post-join validation and no '..' rejection anywhere downstream; os.path.join semantics additionally let an absolute path argument discard base_path entirely. Key taint step from the src attribute value to the open() sink at :86.

Existence oracle only: os.path.exists(file_name) gates the read but returns no file content; the dangerous operation is open() at :86. A TOCTOU-shaped check-then-open window exists between :82 and :86, but the check itself is neither a sink nor a traversal guard.

Extension extraction feeding the image-type whitelist at :84-85; the result selects a MIME type and is never used as a path. The whitelist restricts which files get read, not where they may live - not a traversal guard, and not a sink.

THE B64 read sink: open(file_name, 'rb') reads the file resolved from the attacker-controlled src after decode+join+normpath with no base-directory containment; the content is base64-embedded into the rendered output (data URI), i.e. arbitrary file read plus exfiltration into the generated HTML. Absolute src forms (file://, c:/, //, leading /) read outside base_path by construction.

zipfile.ZipFile(file_location, 'r') opens the archive downloaded from the GitHub zipball_url. The file_location path itself is constrained by the basename+'.zip' composition (see the sanitizer row at :66), but the opened archive is externally sourced content that feeds the unvalidated extractall at :45. Labeled sink conservatively; classification candidate because the source is a semi-trusted HTTPS GitHub API response in a maintainer-run dev tool. Re-examined after the first pass scored 0.5 (<0.55 threshold) and kept at 0.55.

Zip-slip shape: z.extractall(os.path.dirname(file_location)) extracts externally downloaded archive members with NO member-name validation - entry names containing ../ or absolute components would write outside the extraction directory. A real CWE-22 shape, but reachability requires a malicious or compromised GitHub archive response (maintainer tool, semi-trusted source); held at candidate for human review.

os.listdir(base) enumerates the operator-configured tags/<repo> directory to locate the extracted repo folder; base derives from current_dir (a __file__ derivative) and hardcoded repo names, not from attacker input.
Directory test applied to entries listed from the operator tags directory; a type probe on non-attacker paths, not a read/write/delete of an attacker-controlled path.

os.rename(repo_dir, join(base, repo.replace('/', '-'))): the destination is fixed and the source directory name derives from the archive listing (archive-influenced), but renaming within the same operator directory is not a traversal primitive; it is downstream of the same semi-trusted archive as the extractall candidate row.
Existence check on destination = join(current_dir, 'tags', repo.replace('/', '-')) - operator constants only (current_dir from __file__, hardcoded repo names); no attacker-controlled path.
Directory creation of the operator tags destination; constants only, no attacker influence.
shutil.rmtree(destination) removes the operator tags directory before regeneration; destination is built from __file__ derivatives and hardcoded repo names.
Directory re-creation of the same operator destination; constants only.

join(destination, os.path.basename(url) + '.zip') composes the operator destination with a filename that cannot traverse: basename strips all separator components and the literal '.zip' suffix guarantees a flat file name (see the sanitizer row for :66). Not a traversal-capable join; the extraction-column arg_index 0 records the destination operand, the external-derived basename sits in argument 1.

os.path.basename(url) strips every path-separator component from the external zipball_url before the literal '.zip' suffix is appended and joined into the fixed tags directory, so the external URL cannot influence directories - a concrete, implementation-verified neutralization for the download-write path (argument 0 -> result). Held at candidate because it does NOT validate archive members for the extractall at :45, and on POSIX a backslash-containing basename remains a flat (non-separator) filename. Re-examined after the first pass scored 0.5 (<0.55 threshold) and kept at 0.55.

open(file_location, 'wb') writes the downloaded archive bytes to the basename-guarded path inside the fixed tags directory (join at :66 plus the sanitizer row); the write location cannot traverse. If the :66 sanitizer label is rejected at human review, re-evaluate this row together with the join row.

util.parse_url at repl_relative: decodes the attacker href/src value, but the module is verified pure string rewriting - the parsed path is rebuilt into output link text via path2url/urlunparse, never touching the filesystem. Propagation-only local chain, not a Pass 1 sink.
util.url2path at repl_relative: percent-decode of the attribute value feeding the string rewrite at :80-:88; no filesystem access exists in pathconverter.py, so this is not a Pass 1 sink.
os.path.relpath at repl_relative: computes the output-relative display path for the rewritten link; string-only transformation, no file access in the module.
os.path.normpath inside repl_relative's join: lexical cleanup of the composed display path; the result becomes link text, not a file operation.

os.path.join(base_path, path) at repl_relative (argument 1 carries the attacker value): the composed path feeds relpath/path2url and is written back into the output HTML; verified no exists/open/stat anywhere in pathconverter.py, so no Pass 1 sink is reachable.
os.path.normpath(relative_path) on the operator-configured relative path: display-path cleanup for the rewrite; no file access.
util.parse_url at repl_absolute: same as the repl_relative branch - decode feeds a string-only rewrite (:106-:118); no filesystem access in the module.
util.url2path at repl_absolute: percent-decode feeding the string rewrite; no file access.
os.path.normpath over join(base_path, path) at repl_absolute: the normalized path becomes link text via path2url/urlunparse; no file access.
os.path.join(base_path, path) at repl_absolute (argument 1 carries the attacker value): the composed path is rewritten into output link text; module verified string-only, no Pass 1 sink downstream.

os.path.abspath(args.file[0]) canonicalizes the operator's own --file CLI selection; trusted operator input and deliberate access (the file is then fed to the test runner), not a sink for untrusted traversal.

Internal resolution wrapper definition: takes the attacker include path (parameter position 1, self slot included) and returns the first existing os.path.join result across the configured base_path list, with NO validation inside the function (no '..' rejection, no absolute-path rejection, no containment). Required summary step (path parameter -> return value) so taint flows from :258/:276 through the :301 call into codecs.open at :311.

Existence gate on the operator-configured base entry: selects which base is tried, returns no content, and blocks nothing about traversal. Not a sanitizer (a missing file just falls through to the next base) and not a sink.
Type probe distinguishing directory-style from file-style base entries; operates on the operator base value, not the attacker path; not a traversal guard.

THE include-path composition: os.path.join(base, path) with the attacker include path at argument 1 and no post-join validation. os.path.join semantics accept absolute path arguments (discarding base) and pass '..' segments through unchanged; the result is returned by get_snippet_path and opened at :311.

Existence gate on the joined filename: check-then-read with a TOCTOU window before codecs.open at :311, but the check itself returns no content and constrains nothing about where the joined path may point.

os.path.basename is applied to the operator's base entry, NOT to the attacker include path: it supports the file-style base comparison at :169 (case-insensitive basename match) and neutralizes nothing about the user-supplied path. The function name alone does not make this a sanitizer - in this implementation the tainted value never passes through it.
os.path.dirname(base) extracts the directory of the operator base entry for the file-style branch; the attacker path is joined afterwards at :170 with no validation.

Second join branch (file-style base entries): os.path.join(dirname, path) with the attacker path at argument 1 and no post-join containment; identical traversal semantics to :162 (an absolute path argument discards the derived base).
Existence gate of the file-style branch; same check-then-read shape as :163, constrains nothing about traversal.

Call site of the resolution wrapper: self.get_snippet_path(path) inside parse_snippets - argument 0 carries the attacker include path extracted at :258/:276; complements the definition-row summary at :155 so taint propagates into the codecs.open read at :311.

THE Snippets read sink: codecs.open(snippet, 'r', encoding) reads the file resolved from the attacker include path with no base-directory containment - '..' segments, absolute paths (os.path.join semantics) and mixed-separator forms all survive to here; the read lines are recursively re-parsed at :333-341, so nested includes compound the traversal. With the default base_path ['.'] any readable file reachable from the working directory is exposed.

Wrapper definition: path parameter (position 0) -> url2pathname return. Percent-decoding taint step used by b64.py:75 and pathconverter.py:77/:105; needed so taint flows through the helper into the join composition.
urllib.request.url2pathname percent-decodes the path argument: %2e%2e%2f becomes ../ before the joins in the b64 pipeline. Propagation step, explicitly not a sanitizer in this implementation.

Shared decode helper definition: url parameter (position 0) -> 8-tuple return including the path component and the is_absolute flag. html.unescape plus urlparse and backslash-to-slash rewrites in the file:// branches; taint must flow through this return for the b64 pipeline to reach join; the function is a decoder, not a guard.
html.unescape(url) decodes HTML entities (., .) BEFORE parsing and joining - attacker encodings decode into traversal characters downstream of this step. Propagation step, not a sanitizer.
